113179.q: Which hormone stimulates the production of red blood cells and is banned as a doping substance when injected?
113179.e: Erythropoietin (EPO) is produced naturally in the kidney. Given artificially, it is banned in sport.
113179.m: EPO stimulates the production of red blood cells.

113180.q: Which place in the Grisons at over 1,800 metres is known for altitude training?
113180.e: St Moritz is in the Upper Engadine at over 1,800 metres above sea level. Many runners and cross-country skiers train there at altitude.
113180.m: St Moritz is a well-known place for altitude training.

113181.q: What do you often notice during sport in the first few days at high altitude?
a: You get out of breath more quickly
113181.e: Because less oxygen arrives with each breath, you get tired more quickly with the same effort. After a few days, the body gets used to it.
113181.m: At high altitude, you get out of breath more quickly at first.

113182.q: What does the principle “live high, train low” describe?
a: Sleep high up, train lower down
Sleep lower down, train high up
113182.e: You live at altitude so that your blood adapts, but train lower down, where you can train harder.
113182.m: With “live high, train low”, you sleep high up and train lower down.

113183.q: What are health problems such as headaches and nausea when climbing too quickly to high altitudes called?
113183.e: If you climb too quickly to high altitudes, the body cannot adapt. Headaches and nausea are typical signs of altitude sickness.
113183.m: Climbing too quickly can cause altitude sickness.

113184.q: How long does an altitude training camp usually need to last at least to have an effect?
113184.e: The body needs time to make more red blood cells. Altitude training camps therefore often last two to four weeks.
113184.m: Altitude training needs several weeks to work.

113185.q: What is the endurance called that forms the basis for almost all sports and is built up with easy training?
113185.e: Basic endurance allows long efforts at medium intensity. It also helps you recover faster between hard sessions.
113185.m: Basic endurance is the foundation for many sports.

113186.q: What is the ability to adjust quickly to a new situation, for example when the ball bounces off unexpectedly, called?
113186.e: Adaptability lets you change a movement in a flash. It is particularly important in ball games.

113187.q: Why are the wrists particularly at risk when inline skating?
a: Because you often catch yourself with your hands when you fall
Because you move your hands while skating
Because the wheels rub against your hands
Because your hands sweat while skating
113187.e: When you fall, you stretch out your hands by reflex. Wrist guards prevent fractures and grazes when this happens.
113187.m: When inline skating, wrist guards protect against injuries.

113188.q: Why should you warm up your body briefly before stretching?
a: So that your pulse goes down
113188.e: Warmed-up muscles have a better blood supply and are more elastic. They can be stretched more easily and with less risk of injury.
113188.m: Warm muscles stretch better than cold ones.

114063.q: What does the abbreviation REM in REM sleep stand for?
114063.e: REM stands for “Rapid Eye Movement”. In this sleep phase, the eyes move quickly back and forth under the closed eyelids.
114063.m: REM stands for the rapid eye movements during sleep.

114064.q: In which sleep phase do we dream particularly vividly and in pictures?
114064.e: People woken from REM sleep usually report vivid, story-like dreams. Dreams also occur in other phases, but they are usually fainter there.
114064.m: We have our most vivid dreams in REM sleep.

114065.q: What happens to most skeletal muscles during REM sleep?
114065.e: In REM sleep, the skeletal muscles are largely paralysed. This stops us actually carrying out the movements from our dreams.
114065.m: In REM sleep, the muscles are relaxed so that we do not act out our dreams.

114066.q: Why is REM sleep also called “paradoxical sleep”?
a: The brain is almost as active as when awake
You sleep with your eyes open
You do not breathe at all
114066.e: Although the body is deeply asleep, the brain in REM sleep shows a pattern of activity similar to being awake. This apparent contradiction gave the phase its name.
114066.m: In paradoxical sleep, the body is still but the brain is very active.

114067.q: Roughly what share of a night does REM sleep make up in adults?
114067.e: In healthy adults, REM sleep makes up around a fifth to a quarter of sleeping time. We spend most of the night in non-REM sleep.
114067.m: Adults spend about a fifth to a quarter of the night in REM sleep.

114068.q: Who spends a particularly large amount of sleeping time in REM sleep, about half?
114068.e: In newborn babies, active sleep, which corresponds to REM sleep, makes up about half of their sleep. This share decreases as they get older.
114068.m: Babies spend much more time in REM sleep than adults.

114069.q: When in the night do the REM phases last longest?
a: They are always the same length
114069.e: The first REM phase of the night is often only a few minutes long. The REM phases get longer from cycle to cycle, which is why we often remember dreams in the morning.
114069.m: The REM phases get longer and longer as the night goes on.

114070.q: Roughly how many REM phases do you have in a night?
114070.e: A sleep cycle lasts about 90 minutes and usually ends with a REM phase. In one night, you go through 4 to 6 such cycles.
114070.m: There are several REM phases each night.

114071.q: How do heartbeat and breathing typically behave during REM sleep?
114071.e: In REM sleep, pulse and breathing vary more than in calm deep sleep. This fits with the high activity of the brain in this phase.
114071.m: In REM sleep, heartbeat and breathing become more irregular.

114072.q: How do brain waves change in deep sleep?
114072.e: If you measure brain activity in deep sleep, large, slow waves appear. The brain is then particularly calm.
114072.m: In deep sleep, the brain oscillates slowly.

114073.q: In which part of the night is deep sleep most common?
a: In the first half of the night
In the second half of the night
114073.e: The longest deep sleep phases occur in the first sleep cycles. Towards morning there is hardly any deep sleep, but more REM sleep.
114073.m: We get most of our deep sleep in the first half of the night.

114074.q: Which hormone is released in larger amounts mainly during deep sleep?
114074.e: The pituitary gland releases a lot of growth hormone, especially in the first deep sleep phases. It is important for growth and the repair of tissue.
114074.m: In deep sleep, the body releases a lot of growth hormone.

114075.q: How do you usually feel when you are woken from deep sleep?
114075.e: It is hard to wake up from deep sleep, and you need a few minutes to think clearly. This state is called sleep inertia.
114075.m: People woken from deep sleep are often groggy.
